=== FIRST ===
Lecture: Lesson 1.6.1: Cable-Pulley Systems and Relative Motion Kinematic Relations

Section 1: Dependent Kinematics of Interconnected Particles (Cable-Pulley Systems)
- Section Identity: Section 1: Dependent Kinematics of Interconnected Particles (Cable-Pulley Systems)
- Core Understanding: When particles are connected by inextensible cables wrapped around pulleys, the motion of one particle depends directly on the motion of the others. Analyzing dependent motion requires establishing fixed datum lines, defining position coordinates (\\(s_A, s_B, \dots\\)) measured from the datum along each cable segment, writing the total length constraint equation \\(l = f(s_A, s_B, \dots)\\), and taking successive time derivatives to yield velocity constraints (\\(\dot{l} = 0 \implies f(v_A, v_B, \dots) = 0\\)) and acceleration constraints (\\(\ddot{l} = 0 \implies f(a_A, a_B, \dots) = 0\\)).
- Visual-First Explanation: A dual-block cable-pulley system suspended from a fixed ceiling datum. As block A moves downward by distance \\(\Delta s_A\\), cable segment lengths adjust, causing block B to move upward by half that distance (\\(\Delta s_B = -\frac{1}{2}\Delta s_A\\)), driven by the constraint equation \\(s_A + 2s_B = l\\).
- Visual Scene Script: A pulley system with a fixed overhead datum line. Block A is suspended by a single cable segment \\(s_A\\) and Block B is supported by a movable pulley wrapped by two cable segments \\(2s_B\\). As Block A is dragged downward, dynamic position arrows \\(s_A\\) and \\(s_B\\) update live. The system enforces length equation \\(s_A + 2s_B = l\\). Differentiating highlights glowing velocity relation \\(v_A + 2v_B = 0 \implies v_A = -2v_B\\) and acceleration relation \\(a_A + 2a_B = 0 \implies a_A = -2a_B\\).
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive pulley builder with drag handles for Block A, length counter \\(l\\), live position coordinate readouts (\\(s_A, s_B\\)), and real-time velocity/acceleration ratio meters (\\(v_A/v_B = -2\\)).
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students establish fixed datums, formulate kinematic cable length constraint equations, and differentiate them to relate velocities and accelerations in connected mechanical systems.
- Concept Check: In a system where cable length is \\(s_A + 2s_B = l\\), if Block A moves downward at \\(v_A = +4\text{ m/s}\\), what is the velocity of Block B? (Answer: \\(v_A + 2v_B = 0 \implies 4 + 2v_B = 0 \implies v_B = -2\text{ m/s}\\), meaning Block B moves upward at \\(2\text{ m/s}\\)).
- Conceptual Summary: Dependent motion uses fixed datums and cable constraint equations \\(f(s_A, s_B) = l\\); differentiating yields velocity constraint \\(f(v_A, v_B) = 0\\) and acceleration constraint \\(f(a_A, a_B) = 0\\).
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: الحركة المعتمدة (Dependent motion) في أنظمة البكرات والحبال، حركة أي جسم بتبقى مرتبطة ومرتكزة على حركة الأجسام الثانية. عشان نحل أي نظام بكرات: 1) بنحدد خط مرجعي ثابت (Datum)، 2) بنقيس أبعاد الأجسام \\(s_A, s_B\\) من الخط ده، 3) بنكتب معادلة طول الحبل الثابت \\(s_A + 2s_B = l\\)، 4) بنشتق بالنسبة للزمن ونطلع علاقة السرعات \\(v_A + 2v_B = 0\\) وعلاقة العجلات \\(a_A + 2a_B = 0\\).
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(l = s_A + 2s_B + \text{constants} \implies v_A + 2v_B = 0 \implies v_A = -2v_B\\), \\(a_A + 2a_B = 0 \implies a_A = -2a_B\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: الونش أو الأسانسير اللي شغال بكرة مزدوجة، لما الموتور يسحب متر واحد من الحبل، الكابينة بترتفع نص متر بس، لكن بضعف القوة وبنص السرعة!

Section 2: Relative Motion Analysis of Particles
- Section Identity: Section 2: Relative Motion Analysis of Particles
- Core Understanding: When two particles \\(A\\) and \\(B\\) move independently in space, the motion of \\(B\\) relative to \\(A\\) is described by the relative position vector \\(\vec{r}_{B/A} = \vec{r}_B - \vec{r}_A\\). Differentiating with respect to time yields the relative velocity vector equation \\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\), where \\(\vec{v}_{B/A}\\) is the velocity of \\(B\\) as observed from a translating reference frame attached to \\(A\\). Differentiating once more yields the relative acceleration equation \\(\vec{a}_B = \vec{a}_A + \vec{a}_{B/A}\\). Vector addition (via component resolution or triangle law) resolves absolute and relative quantities.
- Visual-First Explanation: Two cars \\(A\\) and \\(B\\) navigating an intersection. From a fixed camera on the ground, position vectors \\(\vec{r}_A\\) and \\(\vec{r}_B\\) locate the cars. A relative position arrow \\(\vec{r}_{B/A}\\) points directly from Car A to Car B. A vector addition triangle visually demonstrates \\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\).
- Visual Scene Script: Particles \\(A\\) and \\(B\\) move on independent paths in a 2D plane. Position vectors \\(\vec{r}_A\\) and \\(\vec{r}_B\\) extend from origin \\(O\\). A dynamic relative vector arrow \\(\vec{r}_{B/A}\\) connects \\(A\\) to \\(B\\), forming vector triangle \\(\vec{r}_B = \vec{r}_A + \vec{r}_{B/A}\\). Differentiating displays velocity vector triangle \\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\) and acceleration triangle \\(\vec{a}_B = \vec{a}_A + \vec{a}_{B/A}\\). Switching view perspective to "Observer at A" freezes \\(A\\) at origin and shows \\(B\\) moving along relative trajectory \\(\vec{r}_{B/A}\\).
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive relative motion scene with coordinate frame switch ("Ground Observer" vs "Moving Observer at A"), velocity sliders for \\(\vec{v}_A\\) and \\(\vec{v}_B\\), and vector sum triangle diagram overlay.
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students construct vector addition triangles for relative position (\\(\vec{r}_B = \vec{r}_A + \vec{r}_{B/A}\\)), velocity (\\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\)), and acceleration (\\(\vec{a}_B = \vec{a}_A + \vec{a}_{B/A}\\)).
- Concept Check: If Car A travels north at \\(v_A = 60\text{ km/h}\\) and Car B travels east at \\(v_B = 80\text{ km/h}\\), what is the magnitude of the relative velocity \\(\vec{v}_{B/A}\\)? (Answer: \\(v_{B/A} = \sqrt{v_B^2 + v_A^2} = \sqrt{80^2 + (-60)^2} = 100\text{ km/h}\\)).
- Conceptual Summary: Relative motion relates independent particles via vector equations: \\(\vec{r}_B = \vec{r}_A + \vec{r}_{B/A}\\), \\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\), and \\(\vec{a}_B = \vec{a}_A + \vec{a}_{B/A}\\).
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: لما يكون عندك جسمين A و B بيتحركوا بشكل مستقل، حركة B بالنسبة لـ A بتتوصف بمتجه الموضع النسبي \\(\vec{r}_{B/A} = \vec{r}_B - \vec{r}_A\\). وبلاشتقاق بنوصل لمعادلة السرعة النسبية المشهورة: \\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\)، ومعادلة العجلة النسبية: \\(\vec{a}_B = \vec{a}_A + \vec{a}_{B/A}\\). نقدر نحل المعادلات دي بسهولة برسم مثلث المتجهات أو بفك المتجهات لـ x و y.
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(\vec{r}_B = \vec{r}_A + \vec{r}_{B/A}\\), \\(\vec{v}_B = \vec{v}_A + \vec{v}_{B/A}\\), \\(\vec{a}_B = \vec{a}_A + \vec{a}_{B/A}\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: لو أنت راكب قطر ماشي بسرعة 100 كم/ساعة ومقعدك ثابت، بالنسبة لشخص واقف على الرصيف سرعتك 100 كم/ساعة، لكن بالنسبة لواحد صاحبيك قاعد جنبك في القطر سرعتك بـ صفر (\\(\vec{v}_{B/A} = 0\\)).

Lec10 (Sec2): "Scene Type: Comparison | Objects: Fixed origin frame O (Ground Observer), translating reference frame attached to Particle A, Particle B, absolute position vectors r_A and r_B, relative position vector arrow r_B/A, velocity vector addition triangle (v_A, v_B, v_B/A) | Actions: Particles A and B travel along independent non-collinear paths; absolute position vectors r_A and r_B extend from origin O; relative vector r_B/A directly connects A to B forming vector sum triangle r_B = r_A + r_B/A; velocity vectors v_A and v_B combine via triangle law to resolve relative velocity vector v_B/A; toggling frame switch freezes A at center and renders relative trajectory of B | Overlays: Vector addition identities r_B = r_A + r_B/A, v_B = v_A + v_B/A, and a_B = a_A + a_B/A | User Interactions: Observer frame toggle switch (Ground Frame O vs Translating Frame A) and independent velocity vector dials for v_A and v_B | Visual Learning Outcome: Student visualizes relative motion vectors, masters reference frame transformation, and constructs vector addition triangles for relative velocity and acceleration | Misconception Correction: Corrects the mistaken subtraction order in relative velocity calculations by visually proving that v_B/A represents the velocity of B minus the velocity of A (v_B/A = v_B - v_A)."
